claims.text: Increased intake of whole grains is inversely associated with type 2 diabetes incidence.
Increased intake of cereal fibre is inversely associated with type 2 diabetes incidence.
Moderate intake of total alcohol (12-24 g/day) is inversely associated with type 2 diabetes incidence compared to no consumption.
Higher intake of red meat is associated with increased incidence of type 2 diabetes.
Higher intake of processed meat is associated with increased incidence of type 2 diabetes.
Higher intake of bacon is associated with increased incidence of type 2 diabetes.
Higher intake of sugar sweetened beverages is associated with increased incidence of type 2 diabetes.

evidence.description: For an increment of 30 g/day, adjusted summary hazard ratio was 0.87 (95% CI 0.82 to 0.93) with high quality of evidence.
For an increment of 10 g/day, adjusted summary hazard ratio was 0.75 (95% CI 0.65 to 0.86) with high quality of evidence.
For an intake of 12-24 g/day v no consumption, adjusted summary hazard ratio was 0.75 (95% CI 0.67 to 0.83) with high quality of evidence.
For an increment of 100 g/day, adjusted summary hazard ratio was 1.17 (95% CI 1.08 to 1.26) with high quality of evidence.
For an increment of 50 g/day, adjusted summary hazard ratio was 1.37 (95% CI 1.22 to 1.54) with high quality of evidence.
Per two slices/day, adjusted summary hazard ratio was 2.07 (95% CI 1.40 to 3.05) with high quality of evidence.
For an increase of one serving/day, adjusted summary hazard ratio was 1.26 (95% CI 1.11 to 1.43) with high quality of evidence.

methodologies.name: Umbrella review of systematic reviews with meta-analyses
methodologies.description: An umbrella review evaluating the strength and validity of summary risk estimates regarding associations between dietary factors and type 2 diabetes incidence.

limitations.text: Few of the associations between dietary factors and type 2 diabetes incidence were graded as high quality of evidence.

future_work.text: More well conducted research, with more detailed assessment of diet, is needed in type 2 diabetes prevention.
